notes: Only assigned unfinished fields were assessed; other fields/sides are null placeholders. Evidence quotes use canonical text; rendered supplied PDF pages inspected for metric/layout. The identical broad description and page-9 locator do not identify an outcome (knowledge gaps versus curiosity), learning phase, main effect versus interaction, or conventional versus multilevel conceptual-learning test. No assignment by row position, requested metric, or numerical matching is justified. Section 8.4 timing candidates: first phase knowledge gaps F[1,228]=87.95, p<.001, partial eta-squared .28; curiosity F[1,228]=40.71, p<.001, partial eta-squared .15; second phase knowledge gaps F[1,227]=10.73, p=.001, partial eta-squared .05; curiosity F[1,227]=7.44, p=.01, partial eta-squared .03. Repeated-measures measurement-point effects: knowledge gaps F[1,230]=116.18, p<.001, partial eta-squared .34; curiosity F[1,223]=110.43, p<.001, partial eta-squared .33. Measurement-point by timing effects: knowledge gaps F[1,230]=41.96, p<.001, partial eta-squared .15; curiosity F[1,223]=15.57, p<.001, partial eta-squared .07. Other form/interaction/posthoc tests also occur in section 8.4. Section 8.2 on the same page reports multilevel conceptual-knowledge timing F[1,91.13]=13.90, p<.001; form F[1,90.43]=32.23, p<.001; interaction F[1,90.38]=3.07, p=.08. None selected. N candidates explicitly printed: 232 first phase, 231 second phase, participants with questionnaire data; missing data reduce the initial sample. No N derived from df, and no group sum assigned.
